 FALMOUTH (WGME) -- A stash of mystery money, found in the woods in Falmouth, will go toward helping families afford their heating bills.
 More than $55,000 was found in a safe behind the central fire station in 2022. The safe was later turned over to Falmouth police, but officers have been unable to find who the money belonged to. It's never been claimed.
 Chief John Kilbride says it's anyone's guess how the safe ended up there. 
 Also read: Maine developer revives plan to turn former Jay paper mill into AI data center 
 “We’re surmising it was there for pickup and something else was going to get dropped off. But we don’t know," Kilbride said.
 Falmouth police say officers were able to trace the cash to a bank in New Hampshire. The bank told them the money was not stolen. The police says it followed protocol, contacted several law enforcement agencies and advertised that it had a large sum of unclaimed cash, but they couldn't crack the case.
 "It was certainly an intriguing way of getting funds. This was not taxpayer money. This was not something that was a product of any thoughtful policy. This was literally a find in the woods," Falmouth Town Council Chair Bryce Hach said. 
 According to state law, the unclaimed money has to be used for a charitable purpose. The Falmouth Town Council voted to divert the funds to the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program, or LIHEAP. Hach says it was a no-brainer.
 Also read: Governor-Elect Hannah Pingree introduces bipartisan transition team 
 Going into peak heating season, the council believes it could go a long way in helping Mainers in a pinch.
 “Knowing how needed these funds are for heating right now, knowing how expensive fuel is for heating and knowing we’re going right into the winter," Hach said. “This was a true gift for our community and one that literally fell in our lap.”
 The money is expected to be available starting in January.
